Full pre-registration sweep on worlds_largest_container_ports_by_2024_teu.
Two-axis taxonomy (BLOCKING / NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE / SUGGESTION ×
factual / structural / scope).

Pay attention to:

(1) **Canonical-source rule INVERSION** for time-series TEU — this
    instance flips the bridges/dams per-entity-wins rule because Lloyd's
    List 2024 is fresher than per-port infoboxes. Verify the inversion
    is honestly documented in decision_log Rule 2 + source_coverage_notes
    + temporal_note, and that it doesn't contradict the bridges/dams
    precedent for static structural metrics.

(2) Universe rule honesty — does source_defined + table_title + db_analog
    + temporal_note coherently describe the "top-20 by 2024 TEU per
    Wikipedia master article" universe?

(3) Source verification — for each of the 20 staged rows, confirm:
    - Wikipedia master article exists at the cited URL
    - 2024 TEU column has the staged value
    - Per-port article exists and supplies the staged Country + City
    - Note any per-port articles with TEU figures that match staged
      (Busan and Long Beach should match; Singapore and LA partial)

(4) Port name normalization: 4 non-'Port of X' exceptions verified
    against Wikipedia article titles? (Qingdao Port, Port Klang, Tanger
    Med, Laem Chabang)

(5) Hong Kong → Country = China (master-list grouping precedent).

(6) Tanger Med naming: per-port article 'Tanger Med' (no hyphen) vs
    master article 'Tanger-Med' (with hyphen). Staged form follows
    per-port article title. Verify the deviation from master is honest.

(7) Antwerp 2022 merger: master uses 'Port of Antwerp' (legacy), but
    'Port of Antwerp-Bruges' post-merger article also exists. Verify
    staging follows master.

(8) Sort order: TEU DESC + Port ASC alphabetical secondary. Two ties
    (12.3 + 9.7) invert master rank — Tanjung Pelepas before Xiamen;
    Long Beach before Suzhou. Verify the alphabetical secondary is
    consistent with bridges/dams precedent.

(9) City values for ambiguous ports:
    - Ningbo-Zhoushan → 'Ningbo' (primary; Zhoushan secondary partner)
    - Tanjung Pelepas → 'Iskandar Puteri' (encompassing municipality)
    - Tanger Med → 'Tangier' (canonical association; port ~45km outside)
    - Jebel Ali → 'Dubai' (emirate-city; Jebel Ali is the port-area)
    Verify per-port-article supports these choices.

(10) Region: curator-assigned closed-vocab; 9 declared, 6 used (East
     Asia, Southeast Asia, Europe, N. America, Middle East, Africa).
     Verify the country-to-region mapping in decision_log Rule 8 is
     internally consistent (e.g., Hong Kong → East Asia per the China
     grouping; UAE → Middle East; Morocco → Africa).

Return condensed verdict block. Append findings to
worlds_largest_container_ports_by_2024_teu.comments.json.

Verdict: Ready, but not clean. Counts by severity: 0 BLOCKING, 2 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. Counts by issue type: factual 0, structural 2, scope-related 0.

Findings:

H1. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) City distinct-count prose is wrong in two active locations.
Evidence: the staged CSV has 20 rows and 20 distinct City values: Shanghai, Singapore, Ningbo, Shenzhen, Qingdao, Guangzhou, Busan, Tianjin, Dubai, Klang, Rotterdam, Hong Kong, Antwerp, Iskandar Puteri, Xiamen, Los Angeles, Tangier, Long Beach, Suzhou, Laem Chabang. curation.json::decision_log Rule 6 and curation.json::normalization_decisions both say "17 distinct cities" while also saying no repeats / each port has its own city. That is internally contradictory and not derivable from the CSV.
Minimal fix: change both active narrative locations from 17 distinct cities to 20 distinct cities. Keep the ambiguous-city examples.

H2. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) draft.temporal_note incorrectly says Region follows the per-port article rule.
Evidence: draft.json::temporal_note says "For non-time-series attributes (Country, City, Region), per-port article wins". That conflicts with curation.json::source_coverage_notes and decision_log Rule 8, which correctly state Region is curator-assigned from a 9-value closed vocabulary, not sourced from per-port articles. The staged Region values themselves are internally coherent; the problem is just the temporal_note sentence.
Minimal fix: change temporal_note to "For non-time-series sourced attributes (Country, City), per-port article wins; Region is curator-assigned via the documented country-to-region mapping." 

Passed checks:
- Universe rule: source_defined + table_title + db_analog + temporal_note coherently describe top-20 container ports by 2024 TEU per Wikipedia's List of busiest container ports master article. The master article states it lists annual TEU throughput, with 2024 as the latest ranking, and its top-20 rows cover Shanghai through Laem Chabang.
- TEU values: all 20 staged TEU values match the master article's 2024 column after converting thousands of TEU to millions and rounding to one decimal: Shanghai 51.5, Singapore 41.1, Ningbo-Zhoushan 39.3, Shenzhen 33.4, Qingdao 30.9, Guangzhou 26.1, Busan 24.4, Tianjin 23.3, Jebel Ali 15.5, Port Klang 14.6, Rotterdam 13.8, Hong Kong 13.7, Antwerp 13.5, Tanjung Pelepas 12.3, Xiamen 12.3, Los Angeles 10.3, Tanger Med 10.2, Long Beach 9.7, Suzhou 9.7, Laem Chabang 9.6.
- Canonical-source inversion: documented honestly in decision_log Rule 2, source_coverage_notes, and temporal_note. It is not a contradiction of bridges/dams because those were static structural metrics, while TEU is an annual time-series metric and the master article's Lloyd's List 2024 column is fresher.
- Source existence and row support: all 21 source URLs resolve. The cited master article supports the top-20 universe and TEU values. Per-port pages support Country + City for the sampled and edge-case rows: Shanghai (China/Shanghai), Singapore (Singapore/Pasir Panjang, city-state single-cell Singapore is defensible), Ningbo-Zhoushan (China; Ningbo & Zhoushan), Shenzhen (China/Shenzhen), Qingdao (port in Qingdao, China), Guangzhou (China/Guangzhou), Busan (South Korea/Busan), Tianjin (China/Tianjin), Jebel Ali (United Arab Emirates/Dubai), Port Klang (Malaysia/Klang district/town), Rotterdam (Netherlands/Rotterdam), Hong Kong (Hong Kong; master country flag PRC supports staged China), Antwerp (Belgium/Antwerp), Tanjung Pelepas (Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia), Xiamen (China/Xiamen), Los Angeles (United States/Los Angeles), Tanger Med (Morocco; 45 km from Tangier), Long Beach (United States/Long Beach), Suzhou (China/Suzhou), Laem Chabang (Thailand/Laem Chabang).
- Current-year TEU matches in per-port articles where expected: Busan 24.4M 2024, Los Angeles 10.3M 2024, Long Beach 9.7M 2024; Singapore has stale infobox 37.2M 2019 but body/current master match 41.1M 2024. This supports the master-wins time-series rule.
- Port-name normalization: the 4 non-"Port of X" forms are honest per article titles: Qingdao Port, Port Klang, Tanger Med, Laem Chabang. Tanger Med without hyphen follows the per-port article even though the master row uses Tanger-Med. Port of Antwerp follows the master legacy row despite the separate post-2022 Port of Antwerp-Bruges authority page.
- Hong Kong Country = China is defensible under the master-list flag/grouping rule; City = Hong Kong preserves the local entity.
- Sort order: CSV is TEU DESC then Port ASC. The two ties intentionally invert master rank by alphabetical secondary: Port of Tanjung Pelepas before Port of Xiamen at 12.3; Port of Long Beach before Port of Suzhou at 9.7.
- Region mapping: 9 declared, 6 used. The country-to-region mapping is internally consistent: China/South Korea -> East Asia; Singapore/Malaysia/Thailand -> Southeast Asia; Netherlands/Belgium -> Europe; United States -> North America; United Arab Emirates -> Middle East; Morocco -> Africa. Hong Kong -> East Asia follows the China grouping.
- Source discovery: the current master article, List of busiest container ports, is the direct Wiki-family universe/ranking source for this query. No stronger Wikipedia list is needed for this staged scope.

Minimal fixes needed:
1. Update decision_log Rule 6 and normalization_decisions: 17 distinct cities -> 20 distinct cities.
2. Update draft.temporal_note so Region is described as curator-assigned, not per-port sourced.
